[[File:Carl Hodges Cusp Conference 2008.jpg|thumb|Carl Hodges presenting at [[Cusp Conference]] 2008, Chicago, Illinois]]

'''Carl N. Hodges''' (March 19, 1937<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gB_SAAAAMAAJ&q=Carl+N.+Hodges+March+19+%2C+1937&pg=PA170|title=Bioconversion: Hearings Before the Subcommittee on Advanced Energy Technologies and Energy Conservation and Technology, U.S. House of Representatives, Ninety-fifth Congress, Second Session, July 15, August 5, 1978|year=1978}}</ref> &ndash; April 3, 2021<ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-breaking/2021/04/06/carl-hodges-accomplished-arizona-climate-scientist-dies-84/7079936002/ Carl Hodges, accomplished Arizona climate scientist, dies at 84 after Alzheimer's diagnosis]. Retrieved April 6, 2021</ref>) was an American [[Atmospheric physics|atmospheric physicist]] and founder of the [[Seawater foundation]]. He was the main driving force behind ideas of using sea canals to [[Irrigation|irrigate]] [[desert]]s.

The idea is to grow sea farms in the artificial sea canals using plants like [[salicornia]] and [[mangrove]], and introducing fish and shrimp. This is thought to be able to resurrect ecosystems, create jobs, wealth and food sources. This has been proposed as a solution for [[starvation]] and even being able to counter the [[effects of global warming]] and [[sea level rise|rising sea levels]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2007/04/hodges200704|title=The Future's Farmer|website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|date=23 April 2007}}</ref>

He was a primary consultant on development of the [[Epcot]] attraction, [[Living with the Land|Listen to the Land]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-10-03|title=Get the Buzz on Epcot's Legacy of Innovation|url=https://d23.com/get-the-buzz-on-epcot-innovation/|access-date=2021-04-08|website=D23|language=en-US}}</ref>
